title: Hyperkalemia risk (RAAS blockade)
message: ACEi/ARB/ARNI can raise potassium, especially when combined with an MRA and in renal dysfunction. Monitor potassium and renal function after start and adjustments.

title: Angioedema
message: A history of angioedema contraindicates ACEi and ARNI. ARNI requires a 36-hour ACEi-free interval (washout) to reduce angioedema risk.

title: Symptomatic hypotension
message: Symptomatic hypotension limits starting and up-titrating ACEi/ARB/ARNI. Start at a lower dose and reassess systolic BP.

title: Renal function on RAAS blockade
message: A rise in creatinine can occur when starting RAAS blockade; a mild, stable increase is usually tolerable. Reassess eGFR/creatinine in 1–2 weeks.

title: Acute decompensation
message: Do not start or increase a beta-blocker during acute decompensation with significant congestion or hypoperfusion. Start once the patient is euvolemic and stable.

title: Bradycardia / AV block
message: Significant bradycardia or advanced AV block limit beta-blocker use. Assess heart rate and ECG before starting/titrating.

title: Hyperkalemia (MRA)
message: MRAs increase the risk of hyperkalemia. Contraindicated with elevated potassium and caution in renal dysfunction. Monitor potassium and creatinine at 3 days, 1 week, then monthly after start/adjustment.

title: Renal function (MRA)
message: Avoid MRA when eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m². Use caution between 30–45 mL/min/1.73 m², with more frequent monitoring.

title: eGFR and SGLT2i initiation
message: The benefit of SGLT2i is maintained across a wide range of renal function. Respect the eGFR threshold for initiation (generally avoid starting at very low eGFR, per label).

title: Euglycemic ketoacidosis
message: Risk of euglycemic ketoacidosis. Hold the SGLT2i during serious acute illness, prolonged fasting or before surgery. Counsel on genital hygiene (mycotic infection risk).

title: Volume depletion (SGLT2i)
message: SGLT2i has a mild diuretic effect; adjust the diuretic dose to avoid volume depletion and hypotension, especially at the start.

title: Hypotension / hypoperfusion
message: SBP < 90 mmHg and/or signs of hypoperfusion suggest low output. Evaluate the need for inotropic/vasoactive support and monitoring — out of scope for this flow (no cardiogenic shock).

title: Severe hyperkalemia
message: Potassium > 6.0 mmol/L requires immediate management and investigation of the cause before/during diuretic intensification.

title: Renal deterioration
message: Low eGFR or significant worsening of renal function during diuresis requires reassessment of the strategy and volume status (decongestion vs. depletion).

title: Electrolyte disturbances
message: Loop diuretics can cause hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia and hyponatremia. Monitor sodium, potassium and magnesium during diuresis.

title: Exclude HFpEF mimics
message: The diagnosis of HFpEF requires exclusion of mimics (e.g., cardiac amyloidosis, infiltrative cardiomyopathies, valvular disease, pericardial disease and pulmonary hypertension) and clinical/diagnostic confirmation.

title: Hemodynamic instability / possible shock
message: Hypotension, hypoperfusion, oliguria, altered mentation or elevated lactate suggest low output/shock. Manage in a monitored setting (ICU/ED) with immediate specialist evaluation.
